title: eq:rankid (and q9-9's rank=4*rho law) is false for structured non-product lambda

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**The exact rank identity `eq:rankid` is FALSE in general; q9-9's law rank $=4\rho^{\ne}$ is also false.**

Theorem `extract` (eq:rankid) asserts
$$\operatorname{rank}\mathbf S_{(m)}=\min\big(4\,r_m^{\mathrm{off}},\,3n\big),\qquad r_m^{\mathrm{off}}=\min_{\widehat\lambda}\operatorname{rank}\widehat\lambda_{(m)}\ (\text{full off-diagonal}).$$
This is **false** for structured non-product $\lambda$.

**Counterexample (verified, $n=5$, mode $1$).** Using the $\lambda$ of the companion issue (q9-12): ordinary-column part rank-one, cells $(\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta)$ arbitrary nonzero. Then $r_1^{\mathrm{off}}=5$ (true min-completion rank of the full off-diagonal), so eq:rankid predicts $\min(4\cdot5,15)=15$. But the **actual** $\operatorname{rank}\mathbf S_{(1)}=9$ (singular values $\approx 1919,1793,1679,1501,72,32,22,19,9,0,\dots$).

The companion law proposed in **q9-9**, $\operatorname{rank}\mathbf S_{(m)}=\min(4\rho^{\ne}_m,3n)$ with $\rho^{\ne}_m=\operatorname{rank}\Lambda'^{(m)}$ (ordinary columns), is **also false** for the same $\lambda$: it predicts $4\cdot1=4$, actual $=9$.

**Why the Appendix "confirms" eq:rankid.** The numerics only sample products and *generic* $\lambda$, for which the identity does hold; the structured non-products that break it are off the generic locus.

**Impact.** The exact identity is not used in the logical chain (only the inequality $\le$ from Step 3 and the threshold from Thm `lower` are used), so this is not by itself fatal. But it shows the organizing invariant $r_m^{\mathrm{off}}$ does **not** govern $\operatorname{rank}\mathbf S_{(m)}$, undermining the framing of Thm `extract`/Appendix. **Action:** delete or restrict eq:rankid to products / generic $\lambda$, and ensure no later step silently relies on the equality (only on the inequality and on the corrected threshold).
